deliverables.title: Stage 1 — a recording to a graded transcript

threads.title: the typist (faster-whisper large-v3)
threads.question: Turns the waveform into words. One candidate, never compared — which is a default, not a decision.

threads.title: the stopwatch (wav2vec2 base, LibriSpeech)
threads.question: Puts a start and an end on every word. The least examined box here: a small model trained on read audiobooks. re-aligning the corrected words needs the corrected words to be right

threads.title: the name-tagger (five arms: pyannote, Sortformer, DiariZen)
threads.question: Says who was speaking when, reading no words at all. Five arms, compared, still undecided.

threads.title: the joiner (Stage 1c)
threads.question: Lays the turn table over the timed words, so every word knows who said it.

threads.title: the corrections (117 rows of a human error log)
threads.question: Turns the human's error log into the corrected reference. Two defects reported 16 Sep. her quotes and bracketed speaker names come through as speech; interjections land at the end of the host turn

threads.title: the grader (psych_asr.evaluate.grade)
threads.question: Reproduces the annotator's own six error labels against the corrected reference, with nobody listening. its numbers move when the reference is rebuilt

threads.title: the grid (4 typists x 2 stopwatches x 5 name-taggers)
threads.question: A cube, not a table: 40 cells from 13 jobs, because five of six labels cannot move along two axes.

threads.title: the scorer (psych_asr.cli.score_arms)
threads.question: Reads the whole cube and says which combination is worth running on the rest of the sessions.
